acceptance.status_reason: THE CAUSE IS MINE AND THE CHECK WAS NOT WEAKENED. I named the ledger slug irpt-ib461-commentary-draft-store-ticket-id-20261011; a slug without a bare eight-digit run would have passed. The collision was MEASURED before the record was written, not discovered after: the pattern matched '20261011' in the slug and was clear against the entry filename, a timestamp, the 12-digit account id, the commit and the S3 version id. Both available fixes are worse than the failure. Editing p157_cells.py is forbidden by the order. Renaming a slug already committed at b6117bd2fb would leave the record's slug disagreeing with the commit that opened the entry, trading a cosmetic failure for a provenance mismatch. Recording a compliant-looking substitute would be recording something untrue about my own act. So the true slug stands and the status does not flip. AC3's own message names an artifact id, an eight-digit token and a bearer token, so its hazard is identifier or credential leakage; a date inside a ledger slug is neither, and the narrow fix offered in row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-S101 is to run the test over the fields where a leak would land rather than over the ledger block. Row IRPT_BCKEND-D2-S101; the issuer owns the criterion and rule 27 L6 lets it amend without a CTO ruling.

mutant.description: Two mutants were planted in a root outside every worktree, holding copies of the record and the check, each with the baseline read first and the revert read after. MUTANT 1 (AC1): live_after was changed to the pre-release digest while end_state stayed APPLIED -- the shape of a release that silently did not land. MUTANT 2 (AC2): the after body of the refused shape was changed to an OK answer -- the shape of a release whose parser stopped refusing. No mutant is offered for AC3 and the reason is stated rather than omitted: it already FAILS on the real record, which demonstrates its discrimination more strongly than a copy could.
mutant.expected: AC1 FAIL on a live_after that contradicts the end state; AC2 FAIL on an after body that differs from the before body
mutant.observed: Baseline first: AC1 PASS, AC2 PASS. MUTANT 1 -> 'FAIL: end_state APPLIED needs live_after cwf6bUEb...' IB157-1-AC1 FAIL; reverted, AC1 PASS again. MUTANT 2 -> 'FAIL: the refused-shape invoke must answer the same REFUSED body before and after' IB157-1-AC2 FAIL; reverted, AC2 PASS again. Both fired on exactly the property they guard.
mutant.provenance_of_this_observation: MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. The mutants were run and their output read, and only then was this block composed. Stated explicitly because this lane did the opposite earlier today on another order -- drafted a mutant's observed line before running it, where the run happened to agree and the agreement was luck rather than method -- and the correction is worth carrying on the face of the next instance rather than only in the log that recorded it.

determinism.method: The digest was established three independent ways before it was believed: the BUILD_ONLY control printed it with nothing uploaded and the source map untouched; head-object on the uploaded object read the same value from S3; get-function-configuration read the same value from the live function after the apply. The refused shape was invoked twice, before and after the apply, and the two answers compared with cmp rather than by eye. The rollback version was re-read for presence AND for still being the latest, with the version count printed as the denominator, because the module takes its version_id from the latest object rather than from a pin.
determinism.observed: All three digest reads: cwf6bUEbPvKkpOtbldaTmzaqst08D/L7DFB32RtJP1A=. Both refused-shape bodies: status REFUSED reason INVALID_REQUEST, byte-identical. Rollback version ToWX4K7J1NpXcwbkf4imLR6Xu0_0aJGn present and IsLatest true at the re-read of 2 versions, its content-sha256 equal to both the live digest and the pair's live-before; after the release it is the second-newest version and still holds the pre-release bytes, so Branch B stays available.
